# Intravenous anesthetics

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Anesthesiology > Drugs > Intravenous anesthetics*

[Original Article Link](/library/vN0A1g)

---

## Summary

Intravenous <u>anesthetics</u> are a group of fast-acting compounds that are used to induce a state of impaired awareness or complete sedation. Commonly used intravenous <u>anesthetics</u> include <u>propofol</u>, <u>etomidate</u>, <u>ketamine</u>, and <u>barbiturates</u> (e.g., <u>thiopental</u>). <u>Propofol</u> is the standard drug for induction of anesthesia and <u>etomidate</u> is most commonly used in cases of <u>hemodynamic instability</u>. <u>Ketamine</u> plays a key role in <u>emergency medicine</u> because of its strong dissociative, <u>sympathomimetic</u>, and <u>analgesic</u> effects. The <u>barbiturate</u> <u>thiopental</u> reduces <u>intracranial pressure</u>, making it useful in patients with high <u>intracranial pressure</u> and/or <u>head trauma</u>. While the characteristics and side effects of intravenous <u>anesthetics</u> are highly dependent on the substance involved, they all share a strong hypnotic effect.




For more information on <u>benzodiazepines</u> and <u>opioids</u>, see the corresponding articles

## Propofol

### Mechanism of action




* Not fully understood; <u>propofol</u> is thought to act as an <u>agonist</u> on <u>GABA<sub>A</sub> receptors</u> and <u>sodium</u> channels of the <u>reticular formation</u>, and as an <u>NMDA receptor</u> inhibitor.

* Rapid onset and recovery





### Effects




* Hypnotic effects

* Antiemetic

* Antipruritic

* <u>Anticonvulsant</u>

* Bronchodilation

* ↓ Intracranial pressure

* No <u>analgesic</u> or <u>muscle relaxant</u> effects





### Side effects




* <u>Hypotension</u> (dose-dependent)

* Respiratory <u>depression</u> (dose-dependent)

* <u>Anaphylaxis</u> (esp. in patients with <u>allergies</u> to soy or egg products )

* <u>Pain</u> on injection

* Propofol infusion syndrome

* Etiology: high doses and prolonged administration of <u>propofol</u>

* Clinical features: severe <u>metabolic acidosis</u>, <u>rhabdomyolysis</u>, <u>renal failure</u>, and/or cardiac failure (often fatal)

* Diagnostics: Patients undergoing prolonged <u>propofol</u> treatment should have <u>triglycerides</u> monitored at least every 3 days, as increased <u>triglyceride</u> levels correlate with development of <u>propofol infusion syndrome</u>.

* Management: discontinue <u>propofol</u> immediately, symptomatic treatment





### Indications




* Standard for anesthesia induction

* Total intravenous anesthesia (<u>TIVA</u>)

* A technique for induction and maintenance of <u>general anesthesia</u> using IV drugs alone.

* <u>Propofol</u> is the drug of choice, especially for patients with an intermediate to high risk of <u>postoperative nausea and vomiting</u> (<u>PONV</u>).





References:[[4]](/library/6BajbM)[[5]](/library/pBaLbM)

## Etomidate

### Mechanism of action




* Enhances <u>GABA<sub>A</sub> receptor</u> function in the <u>reticular formation</u>

* Rapid onset and recovery





### Effects




* Hypnotic effects

* ↓ <u>Intracranial pressure</u>

* <u>Anticonvulsant</u> effects

* Little to no effect on the <u>cardiovascular system</u>  [[2]](/library/mxYVCr)

* No <u>analgesic</u> or <u>muscle relaxant</u> effect





### Side effects




* Transient <u>acute adrenal insufficiency</u> (due to <u>adrenal cortex</u> suppression → reduced <u>cortisol</u> production)

* <u>Postoperative nausea and vomiting</u>

* Painful injection (avoid by administering an <u>opioid</u> prior to injection)

* <u>Myoclonus</u>





### Indications



* Anesthesia for patients with <u>hemodynamic instability</u>

---

## Ketamine

### Mechanism of action




* <u>NMDA receptor antagonist</u>

* Belongs to the arylcyclohexylamines class

* Rapid onset





### Effects




* Dissociative anesthesia: unique <u>anesthetic</u> state with <u>analgesia</u>, intact spontaneous breathing, <u>amnesia</u>, and no complete <u>loss of consciousness</u>

* Strong <u>analgesia</u>

* Bronchodilation

* <u>Sympathomimetic</u> effects: ↑ blood pressure, ↑ <u>heart rate</u>, ↑ <u>cardiac output</u>

* Increases <u>cerebral blood flow</u>





### Side effects




* <u>Nystagmus</u>

* ↑ Oxygen demand and ↑ pulmonary arterial pressure

* ↑ Intracranial pressure due to increased <u>cerebral blood flow</u>

* Acute psychotomimetic effects: <u>disorientation</u>, <u>hallucinations</u>, vivid dreams, nightmares, and/or abnormal <u>EEG</u> (concomitant administration of <u>benzodiazepines</u> is recommended to avoid these effects)

* Rapid injection or high doses can lead to respiratory <u>depression</u>.

* ↑ Salivation





### Indications




* Ideal emergency <u>anesthetic</u> for <u>polytrauma</u> patients and other patients with risk of <u>hypotension</u> (no cardiovascular <u>depression</u>)

* Treatment-resistant <u>asthma</u>

* Short painful procedures (e.g., <u>fracture reduction</u>)

* Treatment-resistant <u>depression</u>  [[3]](/library/wAbhNw)





> [!NOTE]
> <u>Ketamine</u> may be administered via intramuscular injection if <u>IV access</u> is not possible!




References:[[6]](/library/IBaYXM)[[7]](/library/rBafXM)

## Barbiturates

### Agents




* Thiopental

* Methohexital





### Mechanism of action




* Enhanced <u>GABA</u> action → enhanced duration of <u>chloride</u> channel opening and <u>hyperpolarization</u> of postsynaptic <u>neurons</u> → ↓ neuronal excitability in the <u>brain</u>

* High <u>potency</u>, highly-lipid soluble → rapid onset of action due to quick transfer across the <u>blood-brain</u> barrier → brief recovery time due to redistribution into <u>skeletal muscles</u> and <u>adipose tissue</u>





### Effects




* Hypnotic effects

* ↓ Intracranial pressure due to reduced <u>cerebral blood flow</u>

* Little to no <u>analgesic</u> or <u>muscle relaxant</u> effects





### Side effects




* <u>Hypotension</u> (dose-dependent)

* Respiratory <u>depression</u> and/or <u>apnea</u> (dose-dependent)

* <u>Laryngospasm</u>, <u>bronchospasm</u> (due to <u>histamine</u> release)

* <u>Myoclonus</u>

* Painful injection

* <u>Visual hallucinations</u>

* Vivid dreams

* <u>Bradycardia</u>, <u>arrhythmias</u>

* <u>Cytochrome P450</u> induction





### Indications




* IV anesthesia induction;  (esp. short procedures with minimal <u>pain</u> and high risk of <u>raised intracranial pressure</u>)

* Reduction of <u>intracranial pressure</u> for <u>brain edema</u> following trauma or <u>surgery</u>

* Sedation for <u>electroconvulsive therapy</u> (e.g., <u>methohexital</u>)

* <u>Convulsion</u> during or after anesthesia





### Contraindications




* Hypersensitivity

* Severe cardiovascular decompensation; conditions in which a decrease in blood pressure would be hazardous

* <u>Porphyria</u>

* <u>Addison disease</u>

* <u>Liver</u> or <u>kidney</u> disease

* <u>Severe anemia</u>

* <u>Thyroid disorders</u>

* <u>Myasthenia gravis</u>

* <u>Asthma</u>





References:[[8]](/library/sBatXM)
